newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: M-CELL RISES AFTER STRONG YEAR FIGURES.
newsitem.headline: M-CELL RISES AFTER STRONG YEAR FIGURES.

text.p: Shares in South African cellular phone company M-Cell rose on Tuesday after the firm posted good results for the year ended March 31, dealers said.
By about 0905 GMT the stock was up 14 cents at 590 cents with 23,200 shares worth 137,960 rand exchanging hands.
Dealers said the company's move out of the red had spurred interest in the stock.
"I think they are up on the back of their better results. The results are out and they show that M-Cell has turned loss into profit," one dealer said.
The share rose from 550 cents to 576 cents on Friday in anticipation of the firm's strong performance.
M-Cell's headline earnings per share surged to 8.4 cents from a 3.0 cents loss in the previous year.
M-Cell has a 29.5 percent stake in cellular phone network operator MTN Holdings (Pty) Ltd which it expects to drive profits in the current year.
It said MTN would continue to penetrate rural and disadvantaged communities in line with the government's call for a universal telecommunications service.
"As the market reaches its full potential MTN is well positioned to offer an increasing range of quality services to current and new subsribers," M-Cell said in a statement accompanying results.
